decls.name: TauCeti.CliffordAlgebra.filtration
decls.doc:
The degree filtration of a Clifford algebra: `filtration Q k` is the `R`-submodule spanned by
the products `ι Q v₁ * ⋯ * ι Q vₙ` of at most `k` generators, the empty product `1` included.

This is deliberately not the submodule power `LinearMap.range (ι Q) ^ k`, which spans the products
of exactly `k` generators; see `filtration_eq_iSup_pow` for the comparison.
decls.statement: def filtration (Q : QuadraticForm R M) (k : ℕ) : Submodule R (CliffordAlgebra Q)

decls.name: TauCeti.CliffordAlgebra.prod_map_ι_mem_filtration
decls.doc:
A product of at most `k` generators lies in the `k`-th step of the filtration. This is the
generating family, so most `filtration` memberships reduce to it.
decls.statement:
theorem prod_map_ι_mem_filtration {k : ℕ} {l : List M} (hl : l.length ≤ k) :
    (l.map (ι Q)).prod ∈ filtration Q k

decls.name: TauCeti.CliffordAlgebra.filtration_le_iff
decls.doc:
The `k`-th step of the filtration is spanned by the products of at most `k` generators, so a
submodule contains it exactly when it contains those products. This is `Submodule.span_le` in the
form in which it applies to `filtration`.
decls.statement:
theorem filtration_le_iff {k : ℕ} {p : Submodule R (CliffordAlgebra Q)} :
    filtration Q k ≤ p ↔ ∀ l : List M, l.length ≤ k → (l.map (ι Q)).prod ∈ p

decls.name: TauCeti.CliffordAlgebra.filtration_mono
decls.doc:
The filtration is increasing: a product of at most `i` generators is a product of at most `j`
of them whenever `i ≤ j`.
decls.statement: theorem filtration_mono : Monotone (filtration Q)

decls.name: TauCeti.CliffordAlgebra.filtration_zero
decls.doc: The zeroth step of the filtration is the module of scalars, the span of the empty product.
decls.statement: theorem filtration_zero : filtration Q 0 = 1

decls.name: TauCeti.CliffordAlgebra.one_mem_filtration
decls.doc: `1` is the empty product of generators, so it lies in every step of the filtration.
decls.statement: theorem one_mem_filtration (k : ℕ) : (1 : CliffordAlgebra Q) ∈ filtration Q k

decls.name: TauCeti.CliffordAlgebra.one_le_filtration
decls.doc: The submodule form of `one_mem_filtration`: the scalars sit inside every step.
decls.statement: theorem one_le_filtration (k : ℕ) : 1 ≤ filtration Q k

decls.name: TauCeti.CliffordAlgebra.algebraMap_mem_filtration
decls.doc: Scalars lie in every step of the filtration, being multiples of the empty product.
decls.statement:
theorem algebraMap_mem_filtration (r : R) (k : ℕ) :
    algebraMap R (CliffordAlgebra Q) r ∈ filtration Q k

decls.name: TauCeti.CliffordAlgebra.ι_mem_filtration_one
decls.doc: A generator is a product of one generator, so it lies in the first step.
decls.statement: theorem ι_mem_filtration_one (m : M) : ι Q m ∈ filtration Q 1

decls.name: TauCeti.CliffordAlgebra.ι_range_le_filtration_one
decls.doc:
The submodule form of `ι_mem_filtration_one`: all of `LinearMap.range (ι Q)` lies in the first
step.
decls.statement: theorem ι_range_le_filtration_one : LinearMap.range (ι Q) ≤ filtration Q 1

decls.name: TauCeti.CliffordAlgebra.ι_mul_ι_mem_filtration_two
decls.doc:
A product of two generators lies in the second step. This is the membership the roadmap's
bivectors use.
decls.statement: theorem ι_mul_ι_mem_filtration_two (a b : M) : ι Q a * ι Q b ∈ filtration Q 2

decls.name: TauCeti.CliffordAlgebra.filtration_mul
decls.doc:
**The filtration is multiplicative**, and exactly so. Concatenating a product of at most `i`
generators with a product of at most `j` generators gives a product of at most `i + j` of them, and
conversely a product of at most `i + j` generators splits after its `i`-th factor. In particular the
associated graded object of the filtration is an algebra.
decls.title: The filtration is multiplicative
decls.statement:
theorem filtration_mul (i j : ℕ) :
    filtration Q i * filtration Q j = filtration Q (i + j)

decls.name: TauCeti.CliffordAlgebra.filtration_pow
decls.doc:
Iterating `filtration_mul`: the `n`-th submodule power of the `i`-th step is the `i * n`-th
step.
decls.statement: theorem filtration_pow (i n : ℕ) : filtration Q i ^ n = filtration Q (i * n)

decls.name: TauCeti.CliffordAlgebra.prod_map_ι_mem_pow
decls.doc:
A product of exactly `n` generators lies in the `n`-th submodule power of
`LinearMap.range (ι Q)`.
decls.statement:
theorem prod_map_ι_mem_pow (l : List M) :
    (l.map (ι Q)).prod ∈ LinearMap.range (ι Q) ^ l.length

decls.name: TauCeti.CliffordAlgebra.ι_range_pow_le_filtration
decls.doc: The products of exactly `n` generators are among the products of at most `n` of them.
decls.statement: theorem ι_range_pow_le_filtration (n : ℕ) : LinearMap.range (ι Q) ^ n ≤ filtration Q n

decls.name: TauCeti.CliffordAlgebra.filtration_eq_iSup_pow
decls.doc:
The comparison between the filtration and the submodule powers of `LinearMap.range (ι Q)`:
`filtration Q k` collects the products of at most `k` generators, so it is the supremum of the
powers up to `k`. Compare `CliffordAlgebra.evenOdd`, the supremum of the powers whose exponent has
a fixed parity.
decls.statement:
theorem filtration_eq_iSup_pow (k : ℕ) :
    filtration Q k = ⨆ i : {i : ℕ // i ≤ k}, LinearMap.range (ι Q) ^ (i : ℕ)

decls.name: TauCeti.CliffordAlgebra.filtration_succ_eq_sup
decls.doc: The successor step of the filtration adjoins the products of exactly `k + 1` generators.
decls.statement:
theorem filtration_succ_eq_sup (k : ℕ) :
    filtration Q (k + 1) = filtration Q k ⊔ LinearMap.range (ι Q) ^ (k + 1)

decls.name: TauCeti.CliffordAlgebra.filtration_one
decls.doc: The first step of the filtration is the scalars together with the generators.
decls.statement: theorem filtration_one : filtration Q 1 = 1 ⊔ LinearMap.range (ι Q)

decls.name: TauCeti.CliffordAlgebra.iSup_filtration_eq_top
decls.doc:
**The filtration is exhaustive.** Every element of the Clifford algebra is a combination of
products of generators, so it lies in some step.
decls.title: The filtration is exhaustive
decls.statement: theorem iSup_filtration_eq_top : ⨆ k, filtration Q k = ⊤

decls.name: TauCeti.CliffordAlgebra.exists_mem_filtration
decls.doc:
The pointwise form of `iSup_filtration_eq_top`, available because the filtration is a directed
family.
decls.statement: theorem exists_mem_filtration (x : CliffordAlgebra Q) : ∃ k, x ∈ filtration Q k

decls.name: TauCeti.CliffordAlgebra.ι_mul_ι_add_swap_mem_filtration_zero
decls.doc:
The generators of a Clifford algebra anticommute up to the polarization of `Q`, which is a
scalar: the associated graded algebra of the filtration is graded-commutative in degree one, the
symmetric sum `ι Q a * ι Q b + ι Q b * ι Q a` dropping to the previous step of the filtration.
decls.statement:
theorem ι_mul_ι_add_swap_mem_filtration_zero (a b : M) :
    ι Q a * ι Q b + ι Q b * ι Q a ∈ filtration Q 0

decls.name: TauCeti.CliffordAlgebra.involute_mem_filtration
decls.doc:
The grade involution preserves each step of the filtration: it multiplies a product of `n`
generators by `(-1) ^ n`.
decls.statement:
theorem involute_mem_filtration {k : ℕ} {x : CliffordAlgebra Q} (hx : x ∈ filtration Q k) :
    involute x ∈ filtration Q k

decls.name: TauCeti.CliffordAlgebra.reverse_mem_filtration
decls.doc: Reversal preserves each step of the filtration: it reverses the list of generators.
decls.statement:
theorem reverse_mem_filtration {k : ℕ} {x : CliffordAlgebra Q} (hx : x ∈ filtration Q k) :
    reverse x ∈ filtration Q k

decls.name: TauCeti.CliffordAlgebra.map_mem_filtration
decls.doc:
An isometry of quadratic forms respects the degree filtration: it takes a product of generators
to a product of the same length.
decls.statement:
theorem map_mem_filtration (f : Q →qᵢ Q') {k : ℕ} {x : CliffordAlgebra Q}
    (hx : x ∈ filtration Q k) : CliffordAlgebra.map f x ∈ filtration Q' k

decls.name: TauCeti.CliffordAlgebra.fg_filtration
decls.doc:
Every step of the filtration is a finitely generated module as soon as `M` is: the `k`-th step
is generated by the products of at most `k` elements of a generating family of `M`.
decls.statement: theorem fg_filtration [Module.Finite R M] (k : ℕ) : (filtration Q k).FG

decls.name: TauCeti.finrank_real_eq_two_mul_finrank_complex
decls.doc:
A compatible complex module structure forces the real dimension to be twice the complex
dimension. This is the ambient-real-structure form of Mathlib's `finrank_real_of_complex`: that
lemma fixes the real structure to be the one induced by restricting scalars
(`Module.complexToReal`), whereas here `V` already carries an ambient `Module ℝ V` made compatible
via `IsScalarTower ℝ ℂ V` (the situation produced by an almost complex structure).
decls.statement:
theorem finrank_real_eq_two_mul_finrank_complex [Module ℂ V] [IsScalarTower ℝ ℂ V] :
    Module.finrank ℝ V = 2 * Module.finrank ℂ V

decls.name: TauCeti.IsComplexLinear
decls.doc:
A real-linear map `F : V →ₗ[ℝ] W` is complex linear for the pair of almost complex
structures `(J, J')` when it intertwines them: `F ∘ J = J' ∘ F`.
decls.statement: def IsComplexLinear (J : V →ₗ[ℝ] V) (J' : W →ₗ[ℝ] W) (F : V →ₗ[ℝ] W) : Prop

decls.name: TauCeti.IsComplexAntilinear
decls.doc:
A real-linear map `F : V →ₗ[ℝ] W` is complex antilinear for the pair of almost complex
structures `(J, J')` when it anti-intertwines them: `F ∘ J = -(J' ∘ F)`.
decls.statement: def IsComplexAntilinear (J : V →ₗ[ℝ] V) (J' : W →ₗ[ℝ] W) (F : V →ₗ[ℝ] W) : Prop

decls.name: TauCeti.isComplexLinear_iff
decls.doc: Complex linearity restated as its defining commutation equation `F ∘ J = J' ∘ F`.
decls.statement:
theorem isComplexLinear_iff {F : V →ₗ[ℝ] W} :
    IsComplexLinear J J' F ↔ F ∘ₗ J = J' ∘ₗ F

decls.name: TauCeti.isComplexAntilinear_iff
decls.doc:
Complex antilinearity restated as its defining anticommutation equation
`F ∘ J = -(J' ∘ F)`.
decls.statement:
theorem isComplexAntilinear_iff {F : V →ₗ[ℝ] W} :
    IsComplexAntilinear J J' F ↔ F ∘ₗ J = -(J' ∘ₗ F)

decls.name: TauCeti.IsComplexLinear.apply
decls.doc: The pointwise form of complex linearity: `F (J v) = J' (F v)`.
decls.statement:
theorem IsComplexLinear.apply {F : V →ₗ[ℝ] W} (h : IsComplexLinear J J' F) (v : V) :
    F (J v) = J' (F v)

decls.name: TauCeti.isComplexLinear_of_apply
decls.doc: A real-linear map intertwining `J` and `J'` pointwise is complex linear.
decls.statement:
theorem isComplexLinear_of_apply {F : V →ₗ[ℝ] W} (h : ∀ v, F (J v) = J' (F v)) :
    IsComplexLinear J J' F

decls.name: TauCeti.isComplexLinear_arrowCongr_iff
decls.doc:
Raw complex-linearity is preserved and reflected by conjugating source and target along
linear equivalences.
decls.statement:
theorem isComplexLinear_arrowCongr_iff {V₂ W₂ : Type*}
    [AddCommGroup V₂] [Module ℝ V₂] [AddCommGroup W₂] [Module ℝ W₂]
    {F : V →ₗ[ℝ] W} (eV : V ≃ₗ[ℝ] V₂) (eW : W ≃ₗ[ℝ] W₂) :
    IsComplexLinear (eV.conj J) (eW.conj J') (eV.arrowCongr eW F) ↔
      IsComplexLinear J J' F

decls.name: TauCeti.IsComplexAntilinear.apply
decls.doc: The pointwise form of complex antilinearity: `F (J v) = -(J' (F v))`.
decls.statement:
theorem IsComplexAntilinear.apply {F : V →ₗ[ℝ] W} (h : IsComplexAntilinear J J' F) (v : V) :
    F (J v) = -(J' (F v))

decls.name: TauCeti.isComplexAntilinear_of_apply
decls.doc: A real-linear map anti-intertwining `J` and `J'` pointwise is complex antilinear.
decls.statement:
theorem isComplexAntilinear_of_apply {F : V →ₗ[ℝ] W} (h : ∀ v, F (J v) = -(J' (F v))) :
    IsComplexAntilinear J J' F

decls.name: TauCeti.isComplexLinear_id
decls.doc: The identity map is complex linear.
decls.statement: theorem isComplexLinear_id : IsComplexLinear J J (LinearMap.id)

decls.name: TauCeti.isComplexLinear_zero
decls.doc: The zero map is complex linear.
decls.statement: theorem isComplexLinear_zero : IsComplexLinear J J' (0 : V →ₗ[ℝ] W)

decls.name: TauCeti.isComplexAntilinear_zero
decls.doc: The zero map is complex antilinear.
decls.statement: theorem isComplexAntilinear_zero : IsComplexAntilinear J J' (0 : V →ₗ[ℝ] W)

decls.name: TauCeti.IsComplexLinear.neg
decls.doc: The negation of a complex-linear map is complex linear.
decls.statement:
theorem IsComplexLinear.neg {F : V →ₗ[ℝ] W} (h : IsComplexLinear J J' F) :
    IsComplexLinear J J' (-F)

decls.name: TauCeti.IsComplexLinear.neg_neg
decls.doc: Complex-linearity is unchanged after negating both source and target endomorphisms.
decls.statement:
theorem IsComplexLinear.neg_neg {F : V →ₗ[ℝ] W} (h : IsComplexLinear J J' F) :
    IsComplexLinear (-J) (-J') F

decls.name: TauCeti.IsComplexLinear.of_neg_neg
decls.doc:
If a map is complex-linear after negating both endomorphisms, then it was complex-linear
before the sign change.
decls.statement:
theorem IsComplexLinear.of_neg_neg {F : V →ₗ[ℝ] W}
    (h : IsComplexLinear (-J) (-J') F) : IsComplexLinear J J' F

decls.name: TauCeti.IsComplexAntilinear.neg
decls.doc: The negation of a complex-antilinear map is complex antilinear.
decls.statement:
theorem IsComplexAntilinear.neg {F : V →ₗ[ℝ] W} (h : IsComplexAntilinear J J' F) :
    IsComplexAntilinear J J' (-F)

decls.name: TauCeti.IsComplexAntilinear.neg_neg
decls.doc: Complex-antilinearity is unchanged after negating both source and target endomorphisms.
decls.statement:
theorem IsComplexAntilinear.neg_neg {F : V →ₗ[ℝ] W} (h : IsComplexAntilinear J J' F) :
    IsComplexAntilinear (-J) (-J') F

decls.name: TauCeti.IsComplexAntilinear.of_neg_neg
decls.doc:
If a map is complex-antilinear after negating both endomorphisms, then it was
complex-antilinear before the sign change.
decls.statement:
theorem IsComplexAntilinear.of_neg_neg {F : V →ₗ[ℝ] W}
    (h : IsComplexAntilinear (-J) (-J') F) : IsComplexAntilinear J J' F

decls.name: TauCeti.IsComplexLinear.comp
decls.doc: The composite of two complex-linear maps is complex linear.

decls.name: TauCeti.IsComplexAntilinear.comp
decls.doc: The composite of two complex-antilinear maps is complex linear.

decls.name: TauCeti.IsComplexLinear.comp_antilinear
decls.doc: A complex-linear map after a complex-antilinear map is complex antilinear.

decls.name: TauCeti.IsComplexAntilinear.comp_linear
decls.doc: A complex-antilinear map after a complex-linear map is complex antilinear.

decls.name: TauCeti.complexLinearPartLinearMap
decls.doc: The complex-linear-part operator `F ↦ ∂F` as a real-linear map on `V →ₗ[ℝ] W`.
decls.statement:
def complexLinearPartLinearMap (J : V →ₗ[ℝ] V) (J' : W →ₗ[ℝ] W) :
    (V →ₗ[ℝ] W) →ₗ[ℝ] (V →ₗ[ℝ] W)

decls.name: TauCeti.complexAntilinearPartLinearMap
decls.doc: The complex-antilinear-part operator `F ↦ ∂̄F` as a real-linear map on `V →ₗ[ℝ] W`.
decls.statement:
def complexAntilinearPartLinearMap (J : V →ₗ[ℝ] V) (J' : W →ₗ[ℝ] W) :
    (V →ₗ[ℝ] W) →ₗ[ℝ] (V →ₗ[ℝ] W)

decls.name: TauCeti.complexLinearPartLinearMap_apply
decls.doc: The defining formula for `complexLinearPartLinearMap J J'` on an input map.
decls.statement:
theorem complexLinearPartLinearMap_apply (J : V →ₗ[ℝ] V) (J' : W →ₗ[ℝ] W)
    (F : V →ₗ[ℝ] W) :
    complexLinearPartLinearMap J J' F = (2⁻¹ : ℝ) • (F - J' ∘ₗ F ∘ₗ J)

decls.name: TauCeti.complexAntilinearPartLinearMap_apply
decls.doc: The defining formula for `complexAntilinearPartLinearMap J J'` on an input map.
decls.statement:
theorem complexAntilinearPartLinearMap_apply (J : V →ₗ[ℝ] V) (J' : W →ₗ[ℝ] W)
    (F : V →ₗ[ℝ] W) :
    complexAntilinearPartLinearMap J J' F = (2⁻¹ : ℝ) • (F + J' ∘ₗ F ∘ₗ J)

decls.name: TauCeti.complexLinearPart
decls.doc: The complex-linear part `∂F = ½ (F - J' ∘ F ∘ J)` of a real-linear map.
decls.statement:
def complexLinearPart (J : V →ₗ[ℝ] V) (J' : W →ₗ[ℝ] W) (F : V →ₗ[ℝ] W) :
    V →ₗ[ℝ] W

decls.name: TauCeti.complexAntilinearPart
decls.doc: The complex-antilinear part `∂̄F = ½ (F + J' ∘ F ∘ J)` of a real-linear map.
decls.statement:
def complexAntilinearPart (J : V →ₗ[ℝ] V) (J' : W →ₗ[ℝ] W) (F : V →ₗ[ℝ] W) :
    V →ₗ[ℝ] W

decls.name: TauCeti.complexLinearPart_def
decls.doc: The defining formula for the complex-linear part as a linear-map equality.
decls.statement:
theorem complexLinearPart_def (J : V →ₗ[ℝ] V) (J' : W →ₗ[ℝ] W) (F : V →ₗ[ℝ] W) :
    complexLinearPart J J' F = (2⁻¹ : ℝ) • (F - J' ∘ₗ F ∘ₗ J)

decls.name: TauCeti.complexAntilinearPart_def
decls.doc: The defining formula for the complex-antilinear part as a linear-map equality.
decls.statement:
theorem complexAntilinearPart_def (J : V →ₗ[ℝ] V) (J' : W →ₗ[ℝ] W) (F : V →ₗ[ℝ] W) :
    complexAntilinearPart J J' F = (2⁻¹ : ℝ) • (F + J' ∘ₗ F ∘ₗ J)

decls.name: TauCeti.complexLinearPart_apply
decls.doc:
The pointwise formula for the complex-linear part:
`∂F v = 1/2 • (F v - J' (F (J v)))`.
decls.statement:
theorem complexLinearPart_apply (J : V →ₗ[ℝ] V) (J' : W →ₗ[ℝ] W) (F : V →ₗ[ℝ] W) (v : V) :
    complexLinearPart J J' F v = (2⁻¹ : ℝ) • (F v - J' (F (J v)))

decls.name: TauCeti.complexAntilinearPart_apply
decls.doc:
The pointwise formula for the complex-antilinear part:
`∂̄F v = 1/2 • (F v + J' (F (J v)))`.
decls.statement:
theorem complexAntilinearPart_apply (J : V →ₗ[ℝ] V) (J' : W →ₗ[ℝ] W) (F : V →ₗ[ℝ] W) (v : V) :
    complexAntilinearPart J J' F v = (2⁻¹ : ℝ) • (F v + J' (F (J v)))

decls.name: TauCeti.complexLinearPart_add_complexAntilinearPart
decls.doc: The canonical decomposition `∂F + ∂̄F = F`.
decls.statement:
theorem complexLinearPart_add_complexAntilinearPart (J : V →ₗ[ℝ] V) (J' : W →ₗ[ℝ] W)
    (F : V →ₗ[ℝ] W) :
    complexLinearPart J J' F + complexAntilinearPart J J' F = F

decls.name: TauCeti.complexLinearPartLinearMap_add_complexAntilinearPartLinearMap
decls.doc: The complex-linear-part and complex-antilinear-part operators add to the identity.
decls.statement:
theorem complexLinearPartLinearMap_add_complexAntilinearPartLinearMap
    (J : V →ₗ[ℝ] V) (J' : W →ₗ[ℝ] W) :
    complexLinearPartLinearMap J J' + complexAntilinearPartLinearMap J J' = LinearMap.id

decls.name: TauCeti.complexLinearPart_add
decls.doc: The complex-linear part is additive in `F`.
decls.statement:
theorem complexLinearPart_add (J : V →ₗ[ℝ] V) (J' : W →ₗ[ℝ] W) (F G : V →ₗ[ℝ] W) :
    complexLinearPart J J' (F + G)
      = complexLinearPart J J' F + complexLinearPart J J' G

decls.name: TauCeti.complexAntilinearPart_add
decls.doc: The complex-antilinear part is additive in `F`.
decls.statement:
theorem complexAntilinearPart_add (J : V →ₗ[ℝ] V) (J' : W →ₗ[ℝ] W) (F G : V →ₗ[ℝ] W) :
    complexAntilinearPart J J' (F + G)
      = complexAntilinearPart J J' F + complexAntilinearPart J J' G

decls.name: TauCeti.complexLinearPart_smul
decls.doc: The complex-linear part commutes with real scalar multiplication in `F`.
decls.statement:
theorem complexLinearPart_smul (J : V →ₗ[ℝ] V) (J' : W →ₗ[ℝ] W) (c : ℝ)
    (F : V →ₗ[ℝ] W) :
    complexLinearPart J J' (c • F) = c • complexLinearPart J J' F

decls.name: TauCeti.complexAntilinearPart_smul
decls.doc: The complex-antilinear part commutes with real scalar multiplication in `F`.
decls.statement:
theorem complexAntilinearPart_smul (J : V →ₗ[ℝ] V) (J' : W →ₗ[ℝ] W) (c : ℝ)
    (F : V →ₗ[ℝ] W) :
    complexAntilinearPart J J' (c • F) = c • complexAntilinearPart J J' F

decls.name: TauCeti.complexLinearPart_zero
decls.doc: The complex-linear part of the zero map is zero.
decls.statement:
theorem complexLinearPart_zero (J : V →ₗ[ℝ] V) (J' : W →ₗ[ℝ] W) :
    complexLinearPart J J' (0 : V →ₗ[ℝ] W) = 0

decls.name: TauCeti.complexAntilinearPart_zero
decls.doc: The complex-antilinear part of the zero map is zero.
decls.statement:
theorem complexAntilinearPart_zero (J : V →ₗ[ℝ] V) (J' : W →ₗ[ℝ] W) :
    complexAntilinearPart J J' (0 : V →ₗ[ℝ] W) = 0

decls.name: TauCeti.complexLinearPart_neg
decls.doc: The complex-linear part commutes with negation in `F`.
decls.statement:
theorem complexLinearPart_neg (J : V →ₗ[ℝ] V) (J' : W →ₗ[ℝ] W) (F : V →ₗ[ℝ] W) :
    complexLinearPart J J' (-F) = -complexLinearPart J J' F

decls.name: TauCeti.complexAntilinearPart_neg
decls.doc: The complex-antilinear part commutes with negation in `F`.
decls.statement:
theorem complexAntilinearPart_neg (J : V →ₗ[ℝ] V) (J' : W →ₗ[ℝ] W) (F : V →ₗ[ℝ] W) :
    complexAntilinearPart J J' (-F) = -complexAntilinearPart J J' F

decls.name: TauCeti.sq_apply
decls.doc: Applying an almost complex structure twice negates, in pointwise form.
decls.statement: theorem sq_apply (hsq : J ∘ₗ J = -LinearMap.id) (v : V) : J (J v) = -v

decls.name: TauCeti.complexLinearPart_isComplexLinear
decls.doc: The complex-linear part really is complex linear.
decls.statement:
theorem complexLinearPart_isComplexLinear (hJ : J ∘ₗ J = -LinearMap.id)
    (hJ' : J' ∘ₗ J' = -LinearMap.id) (F : V →ₗ[ℝ] W) :
    IsComplexLinear J J' (complexLinearPart J J' F)

decls.name: TauCeti.complexAntilinearPart_isComplexAntilinear
decls.doc: The complex-antilinear part really is complex antilinear.
decls.statement:
theorem complexAntilinearPart_isComplexAntilinear (hJ : J ∘ₗ J = -LinearMap.id)
    (hJ' : J' ∘ₗ J' = -LinearMap.id) (F : V →ₗ[ℝ] W) :
    IsComplexAntilinear J J' (complexAntilinearPart J J' F)

decls.name: TauCeti.isComplexLinear_iff_complexAntilinearPart_eq_zero
decls.doc:
A real-linear map is complex linear exactly when its complex-antilinear part vanishes:
the linear-algebra shadow of "`F` is `J`-holomorphic iff `∂̄F = 0`".
decls.statement:
theorem isComplexLinear_iff_complexAntilinearPart_eq_zero
    (hJ' : J' ∘ₗ J' = -LinearMap.id) (F : V →ₗ[ℝ] W) :
    IsComplexLinear J J' F ↔ complexAntilinearPart J J' F = 0

decls.name: TauCeti.isComplexAntilinear_iff_complexLinearPart_eq_zero
decls.doc: A real-linear map is complex antilinear exactly when its complex-linear part vanishes.
decls.statement:
theorem isComplexAntilinear_iff_complexLinearPart_eq_zero
    (hJ' : J' ∘ₗ J' = -LinearMap.id) (F : V →ₗ[ℝ] W) :
    IsComplexAntilinear J J' F ↔ complexLinearPart J J' F = 0

decls.name: TauCeti.IsComplexLinear.complexLinearPart_eq
decls.doc: A complex-linear map equals its own complex-linear part.
decls.statement:
theorem IsComplexLinear.complexLinearPart_eq {F : V →ₗ[ℝ] W} (h : IsComplexLinear J J' F)
    (hJ' : J' ∘ₗ J' = -LinearMap.id) :
    complexLinearPart J J' F = F

decls.name: TauCeti.IsComplexLinear.complexAntilinearPart_eq_zero
decls.doc: The complex-antilinear part of a complex-linear map vanishes.

decls.name: TauCeti.IsComplexAntilinear.complexAntilinearPart_eq
decls.doc: A complex-antilinear map equals its own complex-antilinear part.

decls.name: TauCeti.IsComplexAntilinear.complexLinearPart_eq_zero
decls.doc: The complex-linear part of a complex-antilinear map vanishes.

decls.name: TauCeti.complexLinearPart_eq_and_complexAntilinearPart_eq_of_decomp
decls.doc:
Uniqueness of the complex-linear/antilinear decomposition: if `F = A + B` with `A` complex
linear and `B` complex antilinear, then `A` and `B` are the canonical parts of `F`.
decls.statement:
theorem complexLinearPart_eq_and_complexAntilinearPart_eq_of_decomp
    (hJ' : J' ∘ₗ J' = -LinearMap.id) {F A B : V →ₗ[ℝ] W}
    (hA : IsComplexLinear J J' A) (hB : IsComplexAntilinear J J' B) (hF : F = A + B) :
    A = complexLinearPart J J' F ∧ B = complexAntilinearPart J J' F

decls.name: TauCeti.complexLinearMaps
decls.doc: The real subspace of complex-linear maps `V →ₗ[ℝ] W` for the pair `(J, J')`.
decls.statement: def complexLinearMaps (J : V →ₗ[ℝ] V) (J' : W →ₗ[ℝ] W) : Submodule ℝ (V →ₗ[ℝ] W)

decls.name: TauCeti.complexAntilinearMaps
decls.doc: The real subspace of complex-antilinear maps `V →ₗ[ℝ] W` for the pair `(J, J')`.
decls.statement: def complexAntilinearMaps (J : V →ₗ[ℝ] V) (J' : W →ₗ[ℝ] W) : Submodule ℝ (V →ₗ[ℝ] W)

decls.name: TauCeti.mem_complexLinearMaps
decls.statement:
theorem mem_complexLinearMaps {F : V →ₗ[ℝ] W} :
    F ∈ complexLinearMaps J J' ↔ IsComplexLinear J J' F

decls.name: TauCeti.mem_complexAntilinearMaps
decls.statement:
theorem mem_complexAntilinearMaps {F : V →ₗ[ℝ] W} :
    F ∈ complexAntilinearMaps J J' ↔ IsComplexAntilinear J J' F

decls.name: TauCeti.isCompl_complexLinearMaps
decls.doc:
For genuine almost complex structures, every real-linear map splits uniquely as a
complex-linear plus a complex-antilinear map: the two subspaces are complementary.
decls.statement:
theorem isCompl_complexLinearMaps (hJ : J ∘ₗ J = -LinearMap.id)
    (hJ' : J' ∘ₗ J' = -LinearMap.id) :
    IsCompl (complexLinearMaps J J') (complexAntilinearMaps J J')

decls.name: TauCeti.Matrix.detRowAlternating_mulVec
decls.doc:
Multiplication by a square matrix scales the standard-basis determinant form by its
determinant.
decls.statement:
theorem detRowAlternating_mulVec [CommRing k] {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    (M : Matrix ι ι k) (v : ι → ι → k) :
    Matrix.detRowAlternating (fun i => M *ᵥ v i) =
      M.det * Matrix.detRowAlternating v

decls.name: exteriorPower.trace_map_of_apply_basis
decls.doc:
If an endomorphism is diagonal in a finite basis, then its trace on the `d`th exterior
power is the `d`th elementary symmetric sum of its eigenvalues.
decls.statement:
theorem trace_map_of_apply_basis (b : Module.Basis I R M) (f : M →ₗ[R] M)
    (a : I → R) (d : ℕ) (hf : ∀ i, f (b i) = a i • b i) :
    LinearMap.trace R (⋀[R]^d M) (map d f) =
      ∑ s : Set.powersetCard I d, ∏ i ∈ (s : Finset I), a i

decls.name: exteriorPower.eq_zero_of_finrank_lt
decls.doc: An exterior power above the rank of a finite free module is zero.
decls.statement:
theorem eq_zero_of_finrank_lt (d : ℕ) (h : Module.finrank R M < d) (x : ⋀[R]^d M) :
    x = 0

decls.name: TauCeti.orthogonalGroupToLinearIsometryEquiv
decls.doc: An orthogonal matrix acts on Euclidean space as a linear isometry equivalence.

decls.name: TauCeti.orthogonalGroupToLinearIsometryEquiv_apply
decls.doc:
The linear isometry equivalence associated to an orthogonal matrix acts by matrix-vector
multiplication in Euclidean coordinates.
decls.statement:
theorem orthogonalGroupToLinearIsometryEquiv_apply
    (A : Matrix.orthogonalGroup ι ℝ) (x : EuclideanSpace ℝ ι) :
    orthogonalGroupToLinearIsometryEquiv A x =
      WithLp.toLp 2 ((A : Matrix ι ι ℝ).mulVec x.ofLp)

decls.name: TauCeti.orthogonalGroupToLinearIsometryEquiv_injective
decls.doc: The conversion from orthogonal matrices to linear isometry equivalences is injective.
decls.statement:
theorem orthogonalGroupToLinearIsometryEquiv_injective :
    Function.Injective
      (orthogonalGroupToLinearIsometryEquiv :
        Matrix.orthogonalGroup ι ℝ → EuclideanSpace ℝ ι ≃ₗᵢ[ℝ] EuclideanSpace ℝ ι)

decls.name: TauCeti.QuadraticMap.orthogonalGroup
decls.doc:
The orthogonal group of a quadratic map: the linear automorphisms of `M` that preserve `Q`.

Mathlib's `Matrix.orthogonalGroup n R` is a coordinate version of this for the standard form on
`n → R`: its matrices preserve `x ↦ ∑ i, x i ^ 2`, and are all of its isometries as soon as `2` is
not a zero divisor in `R`. `QuadraticMap.IsometryEquiv Q Q` is the same underlying set as
`orthogonalGroup Q` (see `orthogonalGroupEquivIsometryEquiv`) but carries no group structure.
decls.statement: def orthogonalGroup (Q : QuadraticMap R M N) : Subgroup (M ≃ₗ[R] M)

decls.name: TauCeti.QuadraticMap.mem_orthogonalGroup_iff
decls.statement:
theorem mem_orthogonalGroup_iff {f : M ≃ₗ[R] M} :
    f ∈ orthogonalGroup Q ↔ ∀ m, Q (f m) = Q m

decls.name: TauCeti.QuadraticMap.map_app_of_mem_orthogonalGroup
decls.doc: The defining property of an orthogonal automorphism, in the form in which it rewrites.
decls.statement:
theorem map_app_of_mem_orthogonalGroup {f : M ≃ₗ[R] M} (hf : f ∈ orthogonalGroup Q) (m : M) :
    Q (f m) = Q m

decls.name: TauCeti.QuadraticMap.isOrtho_iff_of_mem_orthogonalGroup
decls.doc: An orthogonal automorphism preserves orthogonality of vectors.
decls.statement:
theorem isOrtho_iff_of_mem_orthogonalGroup {f : M ≃ₗ[R] M} (hf : f ∈ orthogonalGroup Q) (x y : M) :
    Q.IsOrtho (f x) (f y) ↔ Q.IsOrtho x y

decls.name: TauCeti.QuadraticMap.orthogonalGroupEquivIsometryEquiv
decls.doc:
The orthogonal group of `Q`, as a set, is Mathlib's type of self-isometries of `Q`. The content
of `orthogonalGroup` is the group structure, which `QuadraticMap.IsometryEquiv` does not carry.
decls.statement:
def orthogonalGroupEquivIsometryEquiv (Q : QuadraticMap R M N) :
    orthogonalGroup Q ≃ Q.IsometryEquiv Q

decls.name: TauCeti.QuadraticMap.coe_orthogonalGroupEquivIsometryEquiv
decls.statement:
theorem coe_orthogonalGroupEquivIsometryEquiv (Q : QuadraticMap R M N) (f : orthogonalGroup Q) :
    ⇑(orthogonalGroupEquivIsometryEquiv Q f) = ⇑(f : M ≃ₗ[R] M)

decls.name: TauCeti.QuadraticMap.coe_orthogonalGroupEquivIsometryEquiv_symm
decls.statement:
theorem coe_orthogonalGroupEquivIsometryEquiv_symm (Q : QuadraticMap R M N)
    (e : Q.IsometryEquiv Q) :
    (((orthogonalGroupEquivIsometryEquiv Q).symm e : M ≃ₗ[R] M) : M → M) = ⇑e

decls.name: TauCeti.QuadraticMap.congrAut
decls.doc:
Conjugation by a linear equivalence `e : M₁ ≃ₗ[R] M₂`, as an isomorphism of automorphism
groups: Mathlib's `LinearMap.GeneralLinearGroup.congrLinearEquiv` read through
`LinearMap.GeneralLinearGroup.generalLinearEquiv`.
decls.statement: def congrAut (e : M₁ ≃ₗ[R] M₂) : (M₁ ≃ₗ[R] M₁) ≃* (M₂ ≃ₗ[R] M₂)

decls.name: TauCeti.QuadraticMap.congrAut_apply
decls.statement:
theorem congrAut_apply (e : M₁ ≃ₗ[R] M₂) (f : M₁ ≃ₗ[R] M₁) (m : M₂) :
    congrAut e f m = e (f (e.symm m))

decls.name: TauCeti.QuadraticMap.congrAut_symm_apply
decls.statement:
theorem congrAut_symm_apply (e : M₁ ≃ₗ[R] M₂) (g : M₂ ≃ₗ[R] M₂) (m : M₁) :
    (congrAut e).symm g m = e.symm (g (e m))

decls.name: TauCeti.QuadraticMap.map_orthogonalGroup
decls.doc: Conjugation by an isometric equivalence carries `O(Q₁)` onto `O(Q₂)`.
decls.statement:
theorem map_orthogonalGroup (e : Q₁.IsometryEquiv Q₂) :
    (orthogonalGroup Q₁).map (congrAut e.toLinearEquiv : _ →* _) = orthogonalGroup Q₂

decls.name: TauCeti.QuadraticMap.orthogonalGroupCongr
decls.doc:
Isometric quadratic maps have isomorphic orthogonal groups: conjugation by an isometric
equivalence `e : Q₁ ≃qᵢ Q₂` carries `O(Q₁)` onto `O(Q₂)`.

Over an algebraically closed field every nondegenerate quadratic form of a given rank is isometric
to every other, so this is what makes `O(Q)` depend on the rank alone.
decls.statement:
def orthogonalGroupCongr (e : Q₁.IsometryEquiv Q₂) :
    orthogonalGroup Q₁ ≃* orthogonalGroup Q₂

decls.name: TauCeti.QuadraticMap.coe_orthogonalGroupCongr_apply
decls.statement:
theorem coe_orthogonalGroupCongr_apply (e : Q₁.IsometryEquiv Q₂) (f : orthogonalGroup Q₁) (m : M₂) :
    (orthogonalGroupCongr e f : M₂ ≃ₗ[R] M₂) m
      = e.toLinearEquiv ((f : M₁ ≃ₗ[R] M₁) (e.toLinearEquiv.symm m))

decls.name: TauCeti.QuadraticMap.coe_orthogonalGroupCongr_symm_apply
decls.statement:
theorem coe_orthogonalGroupCongr_symm_apply (e : Q₁.IsometryEquiv Q₂) (g : orthogonalGroup Q₂)
    (m : M₁) :
    ((orthogonalGroupCongr e).symm g : M₁ ≃ₗ[R] M₁) m
      = e.toLinearEquiv.symm ((g : M₂ ≃ₗ[R] M₂) (e.toLinearEquiv m))

decls.name: TauCeti.QuadraticMap.polar_apply_of_mem_orthogonalGroup
decls.doc:
An orthogonal automorphism preserves the polarization of `Q`, because the polarization is
built from `Q` and the additive structure alone.
decls.statement:
theorem polar_apply_of_mem_orthogonalGroup {f : M ≃ₗ[R] M} (hf : f ∈ orthogonalGroup Q) (x y : M) :
    polar Q (f x) (f y) = polar Q x y

decls.name: TauCeti.QuadraticMap.mem_orthogonalGroup_iff_polar
decls.doc:
As soon as `2` acts injectively on the target, preserving the polarization is the same as
preserving the quadratic map: an automorphism is orthogonal exactly when it is an isometry of the
polar bilinear form.

Only injectivity is needed, not invertibility of `2`, so this covers integral forms as well: over
`ℤ`, or more generally whenever `N` is `2`-torsion-free, `2` is not a unit but the polarization
still determines `Q`. When `2` is invertible in `R` the hypothesis is
`(isUnit_of_invertible (2 : R)).isSMulRegular N`. Some such hypothesis is needed: in characteristic
two the polarization forgets `Q` entirely on the diagonal.
decls.statement:
theorem mem_orthogonalGroup_iff_polar (h2 : IsSMulRegular N (2 : R)) {f : M ≃ₗ[R] M} :
    f ∈ orthogonalGroup Q ↔ ∀ x y, polar Q (f x) (f y) = polar Q x y

decls.name: TauCeti.QuadraticMap.specialOrthogonalGroup
decls.doc:
The special orthogonal group: the orthogonal automorphisms of determinant one.

The determinant is Mathlib's `LinearEquiv.det`, which is `1` by convention on a module that is not
finite free; on such a module this subgroup is therefore all of `orthogonalGroup Q`.
decls.statement:
def specialOrthogonalGroup (Q : QuadraticMap R M N) :
    Subgroup (M ≃ₗ[R] M)

decls.name: TauCeti.QuadraticMap.mem_specialOrthogonalGroup_iff
decls.statement:
theorem mem_specialOrthogonalGroup_iff {f : M ≃ₗ[R] M} :
    f ∈ specialOrthogonalGroup Q ↔ f ∈ orthogonalGroup Q ∧ LinearEquiv.det f = 1

decls.name: TauCeti.QuadraticMap.specialOrthogonalGroup_le_orthogonalGroup
decls.statement:
theorem specialOrthogonalGroup_le_orthogonalGroup (Q : QuadraticMap R M N) :
    specialOrthogonalGroup Q ≤ orthogonalGroup Q

decls.name: TauCeti.QuadraticMap.specialOrthogonalGroup_normal
decls.doc: `SO(Q)` is normal in `O(Q)`: inside the orthogonal group it is the kernel of the determinant.
decls.statement:
instance specialOrthogonalGroup_normal (Q : QuadraticMap R M N) :
    ((specialOrthogonalGroup Q).subgroupOf (orthogonalGroup Q)).Normal

decls.name: TauCeti.QuadraticMap.reflectionDual
decls.doc:
The linear functional `y ↦ polar Q v y / Q v` cutting out the hyperplane fixed by the reflection
in `v`. It is normalized so that it takes the value `2` at `v`, which is Mathlib's convention for
`Module.reflection`.
decls.statement: def reflectionDual : Module.Dual R M

decls.name: TauCeti.QuadraticMap.reflectionDual_apply
decls.statement:
theorem reflectionDual_apply (y : M) :
    reflectionDual Q v y = ⅟(Q v) * polar Q v y

decls.name: TauCeti.QuadraticMap.reflectionDual_apply_self
decls.statement: theorem reflectionDual_apply_self : reflectionDual Q v v = 2

decls.name: TauCeti.QuadraticMap.reflection
decls.doc:
The reflection of `M` in the hyperplane orthogonal to a vector `v` of invertible norm:
`y ↦ y - (polar Q v y / Q v) • v`. This is Mathlib's `Module.reflection` for the functional
`y ↦ polar Q v y / Q v`.
decls.statement: def reflection : M ≃ₗ[R] M

decls.name: TauCeti.QuadraticMap.reflection_apply
decls.statement:
theorem reflection_apply (y : M) :
    reflection Q v y = y - (⅟(Q v) * polar Q v y) • v

decls.name: TauCeti.QuadraticMap.reflection_apply_self
decls.statement: theorem reflection_apply_self : reflection Q v v = -v

decls.name: TauCeti.QuadraticMap.reflection_apply_of_polar_eq_zero
decls.doc: The reflection in `v` fixes the hyperplane cut out by `polar Q v`.
decls.statement:
theorem reflection_apply_of_polar_eq_zero {y : M} (hy : polar Q v y = 0) :
    reflection Q v y = y

decls.name: TauCeti.QuadraticMap.reflection_apply_of_isOrtho
decls.doc:
The reflection in `v` fixes every vector orthogonal to `v`. Together with
`reflection_apply_self` this says it is the reflection in the hyperplane `v ^ ⊥`.
decls.statement: theorem reflection_apply_of_isOrtho {y : M} (hy : Q.IsOrtho v y) : reflection Q v y = y

decls.name: TauCeti.QuadraticMap.reflection_mul_self
decls.doc: A reflection is an involution, so it has order dividing two in the orthogonal group.
decls.statement: theorem reflection_mul_self : reflection Q v * reflection Q v = 1

decls.name: TauCeti.QuadraticMap.reflection_inv
decls.doc: A reflection is its own inverse.
decls.statement: theorem reflection_inv : (reflection Q v)⁻¹ = reflection Q v

decls.name: TauCeti.QuadraticMap.reflection_symm
decls.doc: A reflection is its own inverse, as a linear equivalence.
decls.statement: theorem reflection_symm : (reflection Q v).symm = reflection Q v

decls.name: TauCeti.QuadraticMap.reflection_mem_orthogonalGroup
decls.doc:
**Reflections are orthogonal.** These are the generators a Cartan-Dieudonné theorem writes an
orthogonal automorphism as a product of, over a field of characteristic not two, for a nondegenerate
form, in finite dimension; none of that is assumed here. In characteristic two `polar Q v v` is
`2 • Q v = 0`, so `reflection Q v` fixes `v` rather than negating it and is a transvection, which is
why that theorem excludes characteristic two. They are also the image of the generating vectors of
the Pin group under twisted conjugation.
decls.title: Reflections are orthogonal
decls.statement: theorem reflection_mem_orthogonalGroup : reflection Q v ∈ orthogonalGroup Q

decls.name: TauCeti.dominantChamber
decls.doc:
The closed dominant chamber of a base: the weights on which every simple coroot is
nonnegative.
decls.statement: def dominantChamber : Set M

decls.name: TauCeti.openDominantChamber
decls.doc: The open dominant chamber of a base: the weights on which every simple coroot is positive.
decls.statement: def openDominantChamber : Set M

decls.name: TauCeti.mem_dominantChamber
decls.doc: Membership in the closed dominant chamber.
decls.statement:
lemma mem_dominantChamber (x : M) :
    x ∈ dominantChamber P b ↔ ∀ i ∈ b.support, 0 ≤ P.coroot' i x

decls.name: TauCeti.mem_openDominantChamber
decls.doc: Membership in the open dominant chamber.
decls.statement:
lemma mem_openDominantChamber (x : M) :
    x ∈ openDominantChamber P b ↔ ∀ i ∈ b.support, 0 < P.coroot' i x

decls.name: TauCeti.openDominantChamber_subset_dominantChamber
decls.doc: The open dominant chamber is contained in the closed one.
decls.statement:
lemma openDominantChamber_subset_dominantChamber :
    openDominantChamber P b ⊆ dominantChamber P b

decls.name: TauCeti.zero_mem_dominantChamber
decls.doc: The origin is dominant.
decls.statement: lemma zero_mem_dominantChamber : (0 : M) ∈ dominantChamber P b

decls.name: TauCeti.add_mem_dominantChamber
decls.doc: The closed dominant chamber is closed under addition.
decls.statement:
lemma add_mem_dominantChamber {x y : M} (hx : x ∈ dominantChamber P b)
    (hy : y ∈ dominantChamber P b) : x + y ∈ dominantChamber P b

decls.name: TauCeti.smul_mem_dominantChamber
decls.doc: The closed dominant chamber is closed under nonnegative scaling.
decls.statement:
lemma smul_mem_dominantChamber {t : R} (ht : 0 ≤ t) {x : M} (hx : x ∈ dominantChamber P b) :
    t • x ∈ dominantChamber P b

decls.name: TauCeti.add_mem_openDominantChamber
decls.doc: The open dominant chamber is closed under addition.
decls.statement:
lemma add_mem_openDominantChamber {x y : M} (hx : x ∈ openDominantChamber P b)
    (hy : y ∈ openDominantChamber P b) : x + y ∈ openDominantChamber P b

decls.name: TauCeti.smul_mem_openDominantChamber
decls.doc: The open dominant chamber is closed under positive scaling.
decls.statement:
lemma smul_mem_openDominantChamber {t : R} (ht : 0 < t) {x : M}
    (hx : x ∈ openDominantChamber P b) : t • x ∈ openDominantChamber P b

decls.name: TauCeti.ofIdx_smul_notMem_dominantChamber
decls.doc:
A simple reflection carries every point of the open dominant chamber out of the closed
dominant chamber, since it reverses the sign of the corresponding simple coroot.

decls.name: TauCeti.ofIdx_smul_ne_of_mem_openDominantChamber
decls.doc:
No simple reflection fixes a point of the open dominant chamber: it would otherwise stay in
the closed dominant chamber.

decls.name: TauCeti.posCorootSum
decls.doc:
The sum of the coroot functionals indexed by the positive roots, evaluated at `x`. Up to the
factor two this is the pairing of `x` with the Weyl vector on the coroot side; all that is used
below is how it transforms under a simple reflection.
decls.statement: def posCorootSum (x : M) : R

decls.name: TauCeti.posCorootSum_reflection
decls.doc:
A simple reflection changes `posCorootSum` by twice the value of its own simple coroot. The
reflection permutes the positive roots other than its own simple root, and negates that one.
decls.statement:
lemma posCorootSum_reflection {i : ι} (hi : i ∈ b.support) (x : M) :
    posCorootSum P b (P.reflection i x) = posCorootSum P b x - 2 * P.coroot' i x

decls.name: TauCeti.exists_mem_dominantChamber_of_finite_weylGroup
decls.doc:
**Every weight is Weyl-conjugate into the closed dominant chamber**, for a crystallographic
reduced pairing with finitely many roots whose Weyl group is finite. Maximizing `posCorootSum`
along the orbit produces the dominant representative.
decls.title: Every weight is Weyl-conjugate into the closed dominant chamber
decls.statement:
theorem exists_mem_dominantChamber_of_finite_weylGroup (x : M) :
    ∃ w : P.weylGroup, w • x ∈ dominantChamber P b

decls.name: TauCeti.orbit_inter_dominantChamber_nonempty
decls.doc: Every Weyl orbit meets the closed dominant chamber.
decls.statement:
theorem orbit_inter_dominantChamber_nonempty (x : M) :
    (MulAction.orbit P.weylGroup x ∩ dominantChamber P b).Nonempty

decls.name: TauCeti.iUnion_smul_dominantChamber_eq_univ
decls.doc: **The Weyl translates of the closed dominant chamber cover the weight space.**
decls.title: The Weyl translates of the closed dominant chamber cover the weight space
decls.statement:
theorem iUnion_smul_dominantChamber_eq_univ :
    ⋃ w : P.weylGroup, w • dominantChamber P b = (univ : Set M)

decls.name: TauCeti.exists_mem_dominantChamber
decls.doc:
**Every weight is Weyl-conjugate into the closed dominant chamber.** Together with the
uniqueness of that representative this says the closed dominant chamber is a fundamental domain
for the Weyl group.
decls.title: Every weight is Weyl-conjugate into the closed dominant chamber
decls.statement:
theorem exists_mem_dominantChamber [P.IsRootSystem] (x : M) :
    ∃ w : P.weylGroup, w • x ∈ dominantChamber P b

decls.name: TauCeti.coxeterOrder
decls.doc:
The order of the product of the reflections in two roots of Cartan product `c`.

For a finite crystallographic pairing the only products that occur are `0`, `1`, `2`, `3` and `4`.
The first four are the rank-two configurations `A₁ × A₁`, `A₂`, `B₂` and `G₂`, whose products of
reflections are rotations of order `2`, `3`, `4` and `6`. Product `4` means the two roots are
proportional, so the two reflections agree and their product is the identity, of order `1`; this is
in particular the value taken by a root against itself. Every other integer is sent to `0`,
Mathlib's encoding of an infinite order.
decls.statement: def coxeterOrder (c : ℤ) : ℕ

decls.name: TauCeti.coxeterOrder_zero
decls.statement: lemma coxeterOrder_zero : coxeterOrder 0 = 2

decls.name: TauCeti.coxeterOrder_one
decls.statement: lemma coxeterOrder_one : coxeterOrder 1 = 3

decls.name: TauCeti.coxeterOrder_two
decls.statement: lemma coxeterOrder_two : coxeterOrder 2 = 4

decls.name: TauCeti.coxeterOrder_three
decls.statement: lemma coxeterOrder_three : coxeterOrder 3 = 6

decls.name: TauCeti.coxeterOrder_four
decls.statement: lemma coxeterOrder_four : coxeterOrder 4 = 1

decls.name: TauCeti.coxeterOrder_eq_zero_iff
decls.doc:
Outside `{0, 1, 2, 3, 4}` the translation falls back to `0`, Mathlib's encoding of an infinite
order. No such Cartan product occurs for a finite crystallographic pairing; this lemma pins the
value down at the remaining integers, so the five equation lemmas above determine `coxeterOrder`
everywhere.
decls.statement: lemma coxeterOrder_eq_zero_iff {c : ℤ} : coxeterOrder c = 0 ↔ c ∉ ({0, 1, 2, 3, 4} : Set ℤ)

decls.name: TauCeti.coxeterOrder_mem
decls.doc:
On the products that occur for a pair of independent roots, `coxeterOrder` takes the four
dihedral values.
decls.statement:
lemma coxeterOrder_mem {c : ℤ} (hc : c ∈ ({0, 1, 2, 3} : Set ℤ)) :
    coxeterOrder c ∈ ({2, 3, 4, 6} : Set ℕ)

decls.name: TauCeti.two_le_coxeterOrder
decls.doc:
The dihedral values are all at least `2`; in particular none of them is `1`, which is what a
`CoxeterMatrix` demands off the diagonal.
decls.statement: lemma two_le_coxeterOrder {c : ℤ} (hc : c ∈ ({0, 1, 2, 3} : Set ℤ)) : 2 ≤ coxeterOrder c

decls.name: TauCeti.coxeterOrder_le_six
decls.doc:
The dihedral values are all at most `6`; in particular none of them is `0`, so no entry of the
Coxeter matrix of a base is infinite.
decls.statement: lemma coxeterOrder_le_six {c : ℤ} (hc : c ∈ ({0, 1, 2, 3} : Set ℤ)) : coxeterOrder c ≤ 6

decls.name: TauCeti.coxeterOrder_le_three_iff
decls.doc:
The products with at most one edge, namely `0` (no edge) and `1` (a single edge), are exactly
those of Coxeter order at most `3`.
decls.statement:
lemma coxeterOrder_le_three_iff {c : ℤ} (hc : c ∈ ({0, 1, 2, 3} : Set ℤ)) :
    coxeterOrder c ≤ 3 ↔ c = 0 ∨ c = 1

decls.name: TauCeti.coxeterOrder_eq_two_iff
decls.doc: The product `0` is the only one of Coxeter order `2`.
decls.statement:
lemma coxeterOrder_eq_two_iff {c : ℤ} (hc : c ∈ ({0, 1, 2, 3} : Set ℤ)) :
    coxeterOrder c = 2 ↔ c = 0

decls.name: TauCeti.cartanMatrix_mul_cartanMatrix_eq_coxeterWeightIn
decls.doc: The Cartan product of a pair of simple roots is their Coxeter weight.
decls.statement:
lemma cartanMatrix_mul_cartanMatrix_eq_coxeterWeightIn (i j : b.support) :
    b.cartanMatrix i j * b.cartanMatrix j i = P.coxeterWeightIn ℤ i j

decls.name: TauCeti.cartanMatrix_mul_cartanMatrix_eq_zero_iff
decls.doc:
The Cartan product of two simple roots vanishes exactly when the first Cartan entry does: both
entries vanish together, since the zero pattern of a Cartan matrix is symmetric.
decls.statement:
lemma cartanMatrix_mul_cartanMatrix_eq_zero_iff (i j : b.support) :
    b.cartanMatrix i j * b.cartanMatrix j i = 0 ↔ b.cartanMatrix i j = 0

decls.name: TauCeti.cartanMatrix_mul_cartanMatrix_eq_zero_iff_isOrthogonal
decls.doc: The Cartan product of two simple roots vanishes exactly when they are orthogonal.
decls.statement:
lemma cartanMatrix_mul_cartanMatrix_eq_zero_iff_isOrthogonal (i j : b.support) :
    b.cartanMatrix i j * b.cartanMatrix j i = 0 ↔ P.IsOrthogonal (i : ι) (j : ι)

decls.name: TauCeti.cartanMatrix_mul_cartanMatrix_mem_of_ne
decls.doc:
**The Cartan product of two distinct simple roots lies in `{0, 1, 2, 3}`**, so `coxeterOrder`
reads a genuine Coxeter order off it.

Mathlib confines the Coxeter weight of a finite crystallographic pairing to `{0, 1, 2, 3, 4}`, and
the value `4` is attained only by linearly dependent pairs of roots. Distinct simple roots are
linearly independent, which removes it.
decls.title: The Cartan product of two distinct simple roots lies in `{0, 1, 2, 3}`
decls.statement:
theorem cartanMatrix_mul_cartanMatrix_mem_of_ne {i j : b.support} (hij : i ≠ j) :
    b.cartanMatrix i j * b.cartanMatrix j i ∈ ({0, 1, 2, 3} : Set ℤ)

decls.name: TauCeti.cartanMatrix_mul_cartanMatrix_eq_one_iff
decls.doc:
The Cartan product of two distinct simple roots is `1` exactly when both Cartan entries are
`-1`, that is, exactly when the two simple roots are joined by a single edge. Off the diagonal the
entries are nonpositive, so the alternative factorisation `1 * 1` cannot occur.
decls.statement:
lemma cartanMatrix_mul_cartanMatrix_eq_one_iff {i j : b.support} (hij : i ≠ j) :
    b.cartanMatrix i j * b.cartanMatrix j i = 1 ↔
      b.cartanMatrix i j = -1 ∧ b.cartanMatrix j i = -1

decls.name: TauCeti.coxeterMatrixOfBase
decls.doc:
**The Coxeter matrix of a base.** Its entry at a pair of distinct simple roots records the order
of the product of the two corresponding simple reflections, read off their Cartan product by
`0 ↦ 2`, `1 ↦ 3`, `2 ↦ 4`, `3 ↦ 6`; its diagonal entries are `1` because a simple root has Cartan
product `4` with itself.

That the entries really are those orders is the classical rank-two computation, and follows in
general from the Coxeter presentation of the Weyl group, which is not built here; the entry `2` is
checked directly in
`TauCeti.RootPairing.weylGroup.orderOf_ofIdx_mul_ofIdx_eq_two_of_coxeterMatrixOfBase_eq_two`.

The body is not exposed: `TauCeti.coxeterMatrixOfBase_apply` is the entry API.
decls.title: The Coxeter matrix of a base
decls.statement: def coxeterMatrixOfBase : CoxeterMatrix b.support

decls.name: TauCeti.coxeterMatrixOfBase_apply
decls.doc:
The entry of the Coxeter matrix of a base at a pair of simple roots is `coxeterOrder` applied
to the product of the two Cartan entries.
decls.statement:
lemma coxeterMatrixOfBase_apply (i j : b.support) :
    coxeterMatrixOfBase P b i j = coxeterOrder (b.cartanMatrix i j * b.cartanMatrix j i)

decls.name: TauCeti.coxeterMatrixOfBase_mem_of_ne
decls.doc: Off the diagonal the Coxeter matrix of a base takes only the four dihedral values.
decls.statement:
lemma coxeterMatrixOfBase_mem_of_ne {i j : b.support} (hij : i ≠ j) :
    coxeterMatrixOfBase P b i j ∈ ({2, 3, 4, 6} : Set ℕ)

decls.name: TauCeti.coxeterMatrixOfBase_ne_zero
decls.doc:
No entry of the Coxeter matrix of a base is infinite: no pair of simple roots of a finite
crystallographic root pairing generates an infinite dihedral group.
decls.statement: lemma coxeterMatrixOfBase_ne_zero (i j : b.support) : coxeterMatrixOfBase P b i j ≠ 0

decls.name: TauCeti.coxeterMatrixOfBase_le_six
decls.doc:
Every entry of the Coxeter matrix of a base is at most `6`, the order attained by the `G₂`
configuration.
decls.statement: lemma coxeterMatrixOfBase_le_six (i j : b.support) : coxeterMatrixOfBase P b i j ≤ 6

decls.name: TauCeti.coxeterMatrixOfBase_eq_two_iff
decls.doc:
**Two simple roots carry the Coxeter entry `2` exactly when they are orthogonal.** On the
diagonal both sides fail: the entry there is `1`, and no root is orthogonal to itself.
decls.title: Two simple roots carry the Coxeter entry `2` exactly when they are orthogonal
decls.statement:
theorem coxeterMatrixOfBase_eq_two_iff (i j : b.support) :
    coxeterMatrixOfBase P b i j = 2 ↔ P.IsOrthogonal (i : ι) (j : ι)

decls.name: TauCeti.isSimplyLaced_iff_forall_coxeterMatrixOfBase_le_three
decls.doc:
**The Cartan matrix of a base is simply laced exactly when the Coxeter matrix of that base has
all entries at most `3`**, that is, exactly when no two simple roots are joined by a multiple
edge.
decls.statement:
theorem isSimplyLaced_iff_forall_coxeterMatrixOfBase_le_three :
    b.cartanMatrix.IsSimplyLaced ↔ ∀ i j, coxeterMatrixOfBase P b i j ≤ 3

decls.name: TauCeti.RootPairing.weylGroup.orderOf_ofIdx_mul_ofIdx_eq_two_of_coxeterMatrixOfBase_eq_two
decls.doc:
**Where the Coxeter matrix of a base has the entry `2`, the product of the two simple
reflections does have order `2`.** This is the one entry of `coxeterMatrixOfBase` that can be
checked before the Coxeter presentation of the Weyl group is available.
decls.statement:
theorem orderOf_ofIdx_mul_ofIdx_eq_two_of_coxeterMatrixOfBase_eq_two
    (b : P.Base) {i j : b.support} (h : coxeterMatrixOfBase P b i j = 2) :
    orderOf (_root_.RootPairing.weylGroup.ofIdx P (i : ι) *
      _root_.RootPairing.weylGroup.ofIdx P (j : ι)) = 2

decls.name: TauCeti.Matrix.isSimplyLaced_congr
decls.doc:
Transporting simple-lacedness of a square matrix along a relabelling of its index type. This is
a proof helper for `TauCeti.HasCartanType.isSimplyLaced_iff`, so it stays private rather than adding
generic matrix API to this Dynkin-specific file.
decls.statement:
lemma isSimplyLaced_congr {α β : Type*} {A : Matrix α α ℤ} {B : Matrix β β ℤ} (e : α ≃ β)
    (he : ∀ i j, A i j = B (e i) (e j)) : A.IsSimplyLaced ↔ B.IsSimplyLaced

decls.doc: Every diagonal entry of a standard Cartan matrix is `2`.
decls.statement:
lemma cartanMatrix_apply_same (t : DynkinType) (i : Fin t.rank) :
    t.cartanMatrix i i = 2

decls.name: TauCeti.DynkinType.cartanMatrix_apply_le_zero_of_ne
decls.doc: Every off-diagonal entry of a standard Cartan matrix is nonpositive.
decls.statement:
lemma cartanMatrix_apply_le_zero_of_ne (t : DynkinType) {i j : Fin t.rank} (h : i ≠ j) :
    t.cartanMatrix i j ≤ 0

decls.name: TauCeti.DynkinType.cartanMatrix_apply_eq_zero_iff_symm
decls.doc:
The zero pattern of a standard Cartan matrix is symmetric: two simple roots are orthogonal in
one order exactly when they are in the other. With `cartanMatrix_apply_same` and
`cartanMatrix_apply_le_zero_of_ne` this says each standard matrix is a generalized Cartan matrix.
This is the `DynkinType` analogue of `RootPairing.Base.cartanMatrix_apply_eq_zero_iff_symm`.
decls.statement:
lemma cartanMatrix_apply_eq_zero_iff_symm (t : DynkinType) (i j : Fin t.rank) :
    t.cartanMatrix i j = 0 ↔ t.cartanMatrix j i = 0

decls.name: TauCeti.DynkinType.cartanMatrix_B_apply_eq_neg_two
decls.doc:
The double edge of type `Bₙ`: with at least two simple roots, the last two are joined by an
entry `-2`.
decls.statement:
lemma cartanMatrix_B_apply_eq_neg_two {n : ℕ} (hn : 2 ≤ n) (i j : Fin n)
    (hi : (i : ℕ) = n - 2) (hj : (j : ℕ) = n - 1) : CartanMatrix.B n i j = -2

decls.statement:
lemma not_isSimplyLaced_cartanMatrix_B {n : ℕ} (hn : 2 ≤ n) :
    ¬ (CartanMatrix.B n).IsSimplyLaced

decls.name: TauCeti.DynkinType.isSimplyLaced_cartanMatrix_iff
decls.doc:
**A standard Cartan matrix is simply laced exactly when its type is, or the type has rank at
most one.** The second alternative is not redundant. Rank at most one holds for `A 0`, `A 1`, `D 0`
and `D 1` as well, but those types are simply laced anyway, so the types it adds to the first
alternative are precisely `B 0`, `B 1`, `C 0` and `C 1`, whose matrices have no off-diagonal entries
at all and so are vacuously simply laced even though the types are not. Excluding those four is all
that `isSimplyLaced_cartanMatrix_iff_of_valid` needs.
decls.statement:
theorem isSimplyLaced_cartanMatrix_iff (t : DynkinType) :
    t.cartanMatrix.IsSimplyLaced ↔ t.IsSimplyLaced ∨ t.rank ≤ 1

decls.name: TauCeti.DynkinType.isSimplyLaced_cartanMatrix_iff_of_valid
decls.doc:
**Among valid Dynkin types the simply-laced Cartan matrices are exactly those of types `A`, `D`
and `E`.** Validity is what rules out `B 1 = A 1`, whose matrix is simply laced.
decls.statement:
theorem isSimplyLaced_cartanMatrix_iff_of_valid {t : DynkinType} (ht : t.Valid) :
    t.cartanMatrix.IsSimplyLaced ↔ t.IsSimplyLaced

decls.name: TauCeti.DynkinType.cartanMatrix_isSymm_of_isSimplyLaced
decls.doc:
A standard Cartan matrix that is simply laced is symmetric: its off-diagonal entries are `0`
or `-1`, and by `cartanMatrix_apply_eq_zero_iff_symm` which of the two an entry is depends only on
the unordered pair of indices. By `isSimplyLaced_cartanMatrix_iff` the hypothesis holds for every
simply-laced type, and for the degenerate `B 0`, `B 1`, `C 0`, `C 1` besides.
decls.statement:
lemma cartanMatrix_isSymm_of_isSimplyLaced {t : DynkinType} (ht : t.cartanMatrix.IsSimplyLaced) :
    t.cartanMatrix.IsSymm

decls.name: TauCeti.HasCartanType
decls.doc:
A base of a crystallographic root pairing **has Cartan type `t`** when its Cartan matrix agrees
with the standard Cartan matrix of `t` after a single simultaneous relabelling of rows and columns.
Matching without transposing is deliberate: from rank `3` on, `Bₙ` and `Cₙ` are different root
systems with transposed Cartan matrices (`CartanMatrix.B_transpose`), so an unoriented match would
identify them. It does not separate `B 2` from `C 2`, which are the same root system;
`TauCeti.DynkinType.Valid` excludes `C 2`.
decls.statement: def HasCartanType (b : P.Base) (t : DynkinType) : Prop

decls.name: TauCeti.hasCartanType_iff_reindex
decls.doc: Having Cartan type `t`, expressed as a reindexing of matrices rather than entrywise.
decls.statement:
lemma hasCartanType_iff_reindex (b : P.Base) (t : DynkinType) :
    HasCartanType P b t ↔
      ∃ e : b.support ≃ Fin t.rank, b.cartanMatrix.reindex e e = t.cartanMatrix

decls.name: TauCeti.HasCartanType.card_support
decls.doc: The rank of the Cartan type of a base is its number of simple roots.
decls.statement:
lemma HasCartanType.card_support {b : P.Base} {t : DynkinType} (h : HasCartanType P b t) :
    b.support.card = t.rank

decls.name: TauCeti.HasCartanType.isSimplyLaced_iff
decls.doc:
**A base of Cartan type `t` is simply laced exactly when `t` is, or `t` has rank at most one.**
The second alternative adds only the degenerate types `B 0`, `B 1`, `C 0` and `C 1`: the remaining
types of rank at most one, namely `A 0`, `A 1`, `D 0` and `D 1`, are simply laced already.
decls.title: A base of Cartan type `t` is simply laced exactly when `t` is, or `t` has rank at most one
decls.statement:
theorem HasCartanType.isSimplyLaced_iff {b : P.Base} {t : DynkinType} (h : HasCartanType P b t) :
    b.cartanMatrix.IsSimplyLaced ↔ t.IsSimplyLaced ∨ t.rank ≤ 1

decls.name: TauCeti.HasCartanType.isSimplyLaced_iff_of_valid
decls.doc:
**A base of valid Cartan type `t` is simply laced exactly when `t` is**, that is, exactly when
`t` is one of `A`, `D`, `E₆`, `E₇`, `E₈`.

decls.name: TauCeti.inversions
decls.doc: The inversion set of `w`: the positive root indices that `w` sends to negative roots.
decls.statement: def inversions (b : P.Base) (w : P.weylGroup) : Set ι

decls.name: TauCeti.mem_inversions
decls.doc: Membership in an inversion set means being positive and having negative image.
decls.statement:
lemma mem_inversions (i : ι) :
    i ∈ inversions P b w ↔ b.IsPos i ∧ ¬ b.IsPos (P.weylGroupToPerm w i)

decls.name: TauCeti.inversions_eq_inter_preimage
decls.doc:
An inversion set is the intersection of the positive roots with the preimage of the negative
roots.
decls.statement:
lemma inversions_eq_inter_preimage :
    inversions P b w =
      posRoots P b ∩ (P.weylGroupToPerm w) ⁻¹' negRoots P b

decls.name: TauCeti.inversions_subset_posRoots
decls.doc: Every inversion is a positive root.
decls.statement: lemma inversions_subset_posRoots : inversions P b w ⊆ posRoots P b

decls.name: TauCeti.mapsTo_inversions_negRoots
decls.doc: The image of every inversion is a negative root.
decls.statement:
lemma mapsTo_inversions_negRoots :
    MapsTo (P.weylGroupToPerm w) (inversions P b w) (negRoots P b)

decls.name: TauCeti.inversions_eq_empty_iff
decls.doc: An element has no inversions exactly when it sends every positive root to a positive root.
decls.statement:
theorem inversions_eq_empty_iff :
    inversions P b w = ∅ ↔
      MapsTo (P.weylGroupToPerm w) (posRoots P b) (posRoots P b)

decls.name: TauCeti.inversions_eq_posRoots_iff
decls.doc:
Every positive root is an inversion exactly when all positive roots are sent to
negative roots.
decls.statement:
theorem inversions_eq_posRoots_iff :
    inversions P b w = posRoots P b ↔
      MapsTo (P.weylGroupToPerm w) (posRoots P b) (negRoots P b)

decls.name: TauCeti.ncard_inversions_le
decls.doc: The number of inversions is at most the number of positive roots.
decls.statement:
lemma ncard_inversions_le [Finite ι] :
    (inversions P b w).ncard ≤ (posRoots P b).ncard

decls.name: TauCeti.inversions_one
decls.doc: The identity Weyl-group element has no inversions.
decls.statement: theorem inversions_one : inversions P b 1 = ∅

decls.name: TauCeti.ncard_inversions_one
decls.doc: The number of inversions of the identity is zero.
decls.statement: lemma ncard_inversions_one : (inversions P b 1).ncard = 0

decls.name: TauCeti.inversions_ofIdx
decls.doc: A simple reflection has exactly its defining simple root as an inversion.
decls.statement:
theorem inversions_ofIdx {i : ι} (hi : i ∈ b.support) :
    inversions P b (RootPairing.weylGroup.ofIdx P i) = {i}

decls.name: TauCeti.ncard_inversions_ofIdx
decls.doc: A simple reflection has one inversion.
decls.statement:
theorem ncard_inversions_ofIdx {i : ι} (hi : i ∈ b.support) :
    (inversions P b (RootPairing.weylGroup.ofIdx P i)).ncard = 1

decls.name: TauCeti.image_root_inversions
decls.doc: Index-level inversions identify with the positive vector roots sent to negative vector roots.

decls.name: TauCeti.ncard_inversions_eq_ncard_vector_inversions
decls.doc: The number of index-level inversions equals the number of vector-root inversions.
decls.statement:
theorem ncard_inversions_eq_ncard_vector_inversions :
    (inversions P b w).ncard =
      ((P.root '' posRoots P b) ∩ {α | w • α ∈ P.root '' negRoots P b}).ncard

decls.name: TauCeti.reflectionPerm_mem_inversions_sdiff
decls.doc:
Membership criterion for the punctured inversion sets: a positive root other than the
reflecting one stays positive and away from it, so only its image needs to be negative.

decls.name: TauCeti.puncturedInversionsEquiv
decls.doc:
Away from the distinguished simple root, reflection bijects the inversion sets before and
after right multiplication by that simple reflection.

decls.name: TauCeti.mem_inversions_mul_ofIdx_iff_not_mem
decls.doc:
Right multiplication by a simple reflection toggles whether its defining simple root is an
inversion.
decls.statement:
lemma mem_inversions_mul_ofIdx_iff_not_mem {i : ι} (hi : i ∈ b.support) :
    i ∈ inversions P b (w * RootPairing.weylGroup.ofIdx P i) ↔
      i ∉ inversions P b w

decls.name: TauCeti.ncard_inversions_mul_ofIdx
decls.doc:
Right multiplication by a simple reflection changes the number of inversions by exactly
one.
decls.statement:
theorem ncard_inversions_mul_ofIdx {i : ι} (hi : i ∈ b.support) :
    (inversions P b (w * RootPairing.weylGroup.ofIdx P i)).ncard =
        (inversions P b w).ncard + 1 ∨
      (inversions P b (w * RootPairing.weylGroup.ofIdx P i)).ncard + 1 =
        (inversions P b w).ncard

decls.name: TauCeti.height_reflectionPerm
decls.doc:
Reflection in the root indexed by `i` changes the height of `j` by the Cartan integer
`P.pairingIn ℤ j i` times the height of `i`.
decls.statement:
lemma height_reflectionPerm (b : P.Base) (i j : ι) :
    b.height (P.reflectionPerm i j) =
      b.height j - P.pairingIn ℤ j i * b.height i

decls.name: TauCeti.height_reflectionPerm_of_mem_support
decls.doc: Reflection in a simple root subtracts the corresponding Cartan integer from the height.
decls.statement:
lemma height_reflectionPerm_of_mem_support (b : P.Base) {i j : ι}
    (hi : i ∈ b.support) :
    b.height (P.reflectionPerm i j) =
      b.height j - P.pairingIn ℤ j i

decls.name: TauCeti.height_reflectionPerm_lt_iff
decls.doc:
Reflection in a simple root strictly decreases height exactly when the corresponding Cartan
integer is positive.
decls.statement:
lemma height_reflectionPerm_lt_iff (b : P.Base) {i j : ι}
    (hi : i ∈ b.support) :
    b.height (P.reflectionPerm i j) < b.height j ↔
      0 < P.pairingIn ℤ j i

decls.name: TauCeti.exists_mem_support_pos_pairingIn
decls.doc: A positive root has positive Cartan pairing with some simple coroot.
decls.statement:
lemma exists_mem_support_pos_pairingIn [Finite ι] (b : P.Base) {j : ι} (hj : b.IsPos j) :
    ∃ i ∈ b.support, 0 < P.pairingIn ℤ j i

decls.name: TauCeti.exists_mem_support_height_reflectionPerm_lt_aux
decls.statement:
lemma exists_mem_support_height_reflectionPerm_lt_aux [Finite ι]
    (b : P.Base) {j : ι} (hj : b.IsPos j) :
    ∃ i ∈ b.support,
      b.height (P.reflectionPerm i j) < b.height j

decls.name: TauCeti.exists_mem_support_height_reflectionPerm_lt
decls.doc:
A nonsimple positive root admits a simple reflection that remains positive and has strictly
smaller height. This is the positive-root lowering step used by induction on height.
decls.statement:
theorem exists_mem_support_height_reflectionPerm_lt [Finite ι] [IsDomain R]
    [P.IsReduced] (b : P.Base) {j : ι}
    (hj : b.IsPos j) (hj' : j ∉ b.support) :
    ∃ i ∈ b.support, b.IsPos (P.reflectionPerm i j) ∧
      b.height (P.reflectionPerm i j) < b.height j

decls.name: TauCeti.posRoots
decls.doc: The positive roots relative to a base.
decls.statement: def posRoots [CharZero R] (b : P.Base) : Set ι

decls.name: TauCeti.negRoots
decls.doc: The negative roots relative to a base.
decls.statement: def negRoots [CharZero R] (b : P.Base) : Set ι

decls.name: TauCeti.mem_posRoots
decls.doc: Membership in the set of positive roots.
decls.statement: lemma mem_posRoots (i : ι) : i ∈ posRoots P b ↔ b.IsPos i

decls.name: TauCeti.mem_negRoots
decls.doc: Membership in the set of negative roots.
decls.statement: lemma mem_negRoots (i : ι) : i ∈ negRoots P b ↔ ¬ b.IsPos i

decls.name: TauCeti.compl_posRoots
decls.doc: The negative roots are the complement of the positive roots.
decls.statement: lemma compl_posRoots : (posRoots P b)ᶜ = negRoots P b

decls.name: TauCeti.negRoots_eq_compl
decls.doc: The negative roots are the complement of the positive roots.
decls.statement: lemma negRoots_eq_compl : negRoots P b = (posRoots P b)ᶜ

decls.name: TauCeti.disjoint_posRoots_negRoots
decls.doc: No root is both positive and negative.
decls.statement: lemma disjoint_posRoots_negRoots : Disjoint (posRoots P b) (negRoots P b)

decls.name: TauCeti.posRoots_union_negRoots
decls.doc: Every root is either positive or negative.
decls.statement: lemma posRoots_union_negRoots : posRoots P b ∪ negRoots P b = Set.univ

decls.name: TauCeti.mem_posRoots_or_mem_negRoots
decls.doc: Every root is either positive or negative.
decls.statement: lemma mem_posRoots_or_mem_negRoots (i : ι) : i ∈ posRoots P b ∨ i ∈ negRoots P b

decls.name: TauCeti.not_mem_posRoots_iff_mem_negRoots
decls.doc: A root is negative exactly when it is not positive.
decls.statement:
lemma not_mem_posRoots_iff_mem_negRoots (i : ι) :
    i ∉ posRoots P b ↔ i ∈ negRoots P b

decls.name: TauCeti.posRoots_finite
decls.doc: The positive roots form a finite set when the root index type is finite.
decls.statement: lemma posRoots_finite [Finite ι] : (posRoots P b).Finite

decls.name: TauCeti.negRoots_finite
decls.doc: The negative roots form a finite set when the root index type is finite.
decls.statement: lemma negRoots_finite [Finite ι] : (negRoots P b).Finite

decls.name: TauCeti.support_subset_posRoots
decls.doc: Every simple root is positive.
decls.statement: lemma support_subset_posRoots : ↑b.support ⊆ posRoots P b

decls.name: TauCeti.posRoots_nonempty
decls.doc: A nonempty root index type has a positive root.
decls.statement: lemma posRoots_nonempty [Nonempty ι] : (posRoots P b).Nonempty

decls.name: TauCeti.reflectionPerm_self_mem_negRoots_iff_mem_posRoots
decls.doc: The negative of a positive root is negative.
decls.statement:
lemma reflectionPerm_self_mem_negRoots_iff_mem_posRoots (i : ι) :
    P.reflectionPerm i i ∈ negRoots P b ↔ i ∈ posRoots P b

decls.name: TauCeti.isPos_reflectionPerm_self_iff_mem_negRoots
decls.doc: The self-reflection of a root is positive exactly when the root is negative.
decls.statement:
lemma isPos_reflectionPerm_self_iff_mem_negRoots (i : ι) :
    b.IsPos (P.reflectionPerm i i) ↔ i ∈ negRoots P b

decls.name: TauCeti.reflectionPerm_self_mem_posRoots_iff_mem_negRoots
decls.doc: The negative of a negative root is positive.
decls.statement:
lemma reflectionPerm_self_mem_posRoots_iff_mem_negRoots (i : ι) :
    P.reflectionPerm i i ∈ posRoots P b ↔ i ∈ negRoots P b

decls.name: TauCeti.exists_root_eq_sum_nat_of_mem_posRoots
decls.doc: A positive root is a nonnegative natural-number combination of simple roots.
decls.statement:
lemma exists_root_eq_sum_nat_of_mem_posRoots {i : ι} (hi : i ∈ posRoots P b) :
    ∃ f : ι → ℕ, f.support ⊆ b.support ∧
      P.root i = ∑ j ∈ b.support, f j • P.root j

decls.name: TauCeti.image_reflectionPerm_self_posRoots
decls.doc: Root negation exchanges positive and negative roots.
decls.statement:
theorem image_reflectionPerm_self_posRoots :
    (fun i ↦ P.reflectionPerm i i) '' posRoots P b = negRoots P b

decls.name: TauCeti.image_reflectionPerm_self_negRoots
decls.doc: Root negation exchanges negative and positive roots.
decls.statement:
theorem image_reflectionPerm_self_negRoots :
    (fun i ↦ P.reflectionPerm i i) '' negRoots P b = posRoots P b

decls.name: TauCeti.reflectionPerm_ne_of_mem_posRoots
decls.doc:
Reflecting a positive root in a simple root never produces that simple root: the only root
sent to a simple root `αᵢ` by `sᵢ` is `-αᵢ`, which is negative.
decls.statement:
lemma reflectionPerm_ne_of_mem_posRoots {i j : ι} (hi : i ∈ b.support)
    (hj : j ∈ posRoots P b) :
    P.reflectionPerm i j ≠ i

decls.name: TauCeti.reflectionPerm_mem_posRoots_diff_singleton_iff
decls.doc:
A simple reflection preserves the set of positive roots other than its own simple root. Both
directions follow from the forward implication because `P.reflectionPerm i` is an involution.
decls.statement:
lemma reflectionPerm_mem_posRoots_diff_singleton_iff {i : ι} (hi : i ∈ b.support) (j : ι) :
    P.reflectionPerm i j ∈ posRoots P b \ {i} ↔ j ∈ posRoots P b \ {i}

decls.name: TauCeti.bijOn_reflectionPerm_posRoots_diff_singleton
decls.doc: A simple reflection permutes the positive roots other than its own simple root.
decls.statement:
theorem bijOn_reflectionPerm_posRoots_diff_singleton {i : ι} (hi : i ∈ b.support) :
    Set.BijOn (P.reflectionPerm i) (posRoots P b \ {i}) (posRoots P b \ {i})

decls.name: TauCeti.image_reflectionPerm_posRoots_diff_singleton
decls.doc:
The image form of `bijOn_reflectionPerm_posRoots_diff_singleton`: a simple reflection maps the
positive roots other than its own simple root onto themselves.
decls.statement:
theorem image_reflectionPerm_posRoots_diff_singleton {i : ι} (hi : i ∈ b.support) :
    P.reflectionPerm i '' (posRoots P b \ {i}) = posRoots P b \ {i}

decls.name: TauCeti.ofIdx_reflectionPerm_eq
decls.statement:
lemma ofIdx_reflectionPerm_eq (i j : ι) :
    RootPairing.weylGroup.ofIdx P (P.reflectionPerm j i) =
      RootPairing.weylGroup.ofIdx P j * RootPairing.weylGroup.ofIdx P i *
        RootPairing.weylGroup.ofIdx P j

decls.name: TauCeti.ofIdx_reflectionPerm_self_eq
decls.statement:
lemma ofIdx_reflectionPerm_self_eq (i : ι) :
    RootPairing.weylGroup.ofIdx P (P.reflectionPerm i i) =
    RootPairing.weylGroup.ofIdx P i

decls.name: TauCeti.ofIdx_mem_closure_simple
decls.statement:
lemma ofIdx_mem_closure_simple (i : ι) :
    RootPairing.weylGroup.ofIdx P i ∈
      Subgroup.closure (range fun j : b.support =>
        RootPairing.weylGroup.ofIdx P (j : ι))

decls.name: TauCeti.weylGroup_eq_closure_simple
decls.doc: The simple reflections associated to a base generate the Weyl group.
decls.statement:
theorem weylGroup_eq_closure_simple :
    (⊤ : Subgroup P.weylGroup) =
      Subgroup.closure (range fun i : b.support =>
        RootPairing.weylGroup.ofIdx P (i : ι))

decls.name: TauCeti.exists_list_prod_ofIdx_eq
decls.doc: Every Weyl-group element is a product of a finite list of simple reflections.
decls.statement:
theorem exists_list_prod_ofIdx_eq (w : P.weylGroup) :
    ∃ l : List b.support,
      (l.map fun (i : b.support) => RootPairing.weylGroup.ofIdx P (i : ι)).prod = w

decls.name: TauCeti.RootPairing.weylGroup.ofIdx_ne_ofIdx_of_ne
decls.doc:
Distinct simple roots give distinct simple reflections: the two reflections already disagree on
the second simple root, since the two simple roots are linearly independent.
decls.statement:
theorem ofIdx_ne_ofIdx_of_ne [NeZero (2 : R)] {i j : ι} (hi : i ∈ b.support) (hj : j ∈ b.support)
    (hij : i ≠ j) :
    _root_.RootPairing.weylGroup.ofIdx P i ≠ _root_.RootPairing.weylGroup.ofIdx P j

decls.name: TauCeti.RootPairing.Equiv.indexHom_injective_of_span_eq_top
decls.doc:
If the roots span, an automorphism of a root pairing is determined by its permutation of the
root indices.
decls.statement:
theorem indexHom_injective_of_span_eq_top (hspan : Submodule.span R (range P.root) = ⊤) :
    Function.Injective (_root_.RootPairing.Equiv.indexHom P)

decls.name: TauCeti.RootPairing.Equiv.indexHom_injective
decls.doc: An automorphism of a root system is determined by its permutation of the root indices.
decls.statement:
theorem indexHom_injective [P.IsRootSystem] :
    Function.Injective (_root_.RootPairing.Equiv.indexHom P)

decls.name: TauCeti.RootPairing.coroot'_reflectionPerm_self
decls.doc: Reflecting a root in itself negates its coroot functional.
decls.statement: lemma coroot'_reflectionPerm_self (i : ι) : P.coroot' (P.reflectionPerm i i) = -P.coroot' i

decls.name: TauCeti.RootPairing.coroot'_reflection_self
decls.doc: A reflection reverses the sign of its own coroot functional.
decls.statement:
lemma coroot'_reflection_self (i : ι) (x : M) :
    P.coroot' i (P.reflection i x) = -P.coroot' i x

decls.name: TauCeti.RootPairing.weylGroupToPerm_injective_of_span_eq_top
decls.doc: If the roots span, the action of the Weyl group on root indices is faithful.
decls.statement:
theorem weylGroupToPerm_injective_of_span_eq_top
    (hspan : Submodule.span R (range P.root) = ⊤) :
    Function.Injective P.weylGroupToPerm

decls.name: TauCeti.RootPairing.weylGroupToPerm_injective
decls.doc: The action of the Weyl group on root indices is faithful.
decls.statement: theorem weylGroupToPerm_injective [P.IsRootSystem] : Function.Injective P.weylGroupToPerm

decls.name: TauCeti.RootPairing.weylGroupToPerm_ofIdx_apply
decls.doc:
The Weyl-group permutation of a simple reflection is the corresponding root-index
reflection.
decls.statement:
lemma weylGroupToPerm_ofIdx_apply (i j : ι) :
    P.weylGroupToPerm (_root_.RootPairing.weylGroup.ofIdx P i) j =
      P.reflectionPerm i j

decls.name: TauCeti.RootPairing.weylGroupToPerm_mul_ofIdx_apply
decls.doc: Right multiplication by a simple reflection acts by first reflecting the root index.
decls.statement:
lemma weylGroupToPerm_mul_ofIdx_apply (w : P.weylGroup) (i j : ι) :
    P.weylGroupToPerm (w * _root_.RootPairing.weylGroup.ofIdx P i) j =
      P.weylGroupToPerm w (P.reflectionPerm i j)

decls.name: TauCeti.RootPairing.weylGroupToPerm_neg
decls.doc: The Weyl-group action on root indices commutes with root negation.
decls.statement:
lemma weylGroupToPerm_neg (w : P.weylGroup) (j : ι) :
    letI

decls.name: TauCeti.RootPairing.weylGroup.coe_ofIdx
decls.doc: A simple reflection of the Weyl group is the corresponding reflection of the root pairing.
decls.statement:
lemma coe_ofIdx (i : ι) :
    ((_root_.RootPairing.weylGroup.ofIdx P i : P.weylGroup) : P.Aut) =
      _root_.RootPairing.Equiv.reflection P i

decls.name: TauCeti.RootPairing.weylGroup.ofIdx_inv_eq
decls.doc: A simple reflection of the Weyl group is its own inverse.
decls.statement:
lemma ofIdx_inv_eq (i : ι) :
    (_root_.RootPairing.weylGroup.ofIdx P i)⁻¹ = _root_.RootPairing.weylGroup.ofIdx P i

decls.name: TauCeti.RootPairing.weylGroup.ofIdx_mul_self
decls.doc: A simple reflection of the Weyl group is an involution.
decls.statement:
lemma ofIdx_mul_self (i : ι) :
    _root_.RootPairing.weylGroup.ofIdx P i * _root_.RootPairing.weylGroup.ofIdx P i = 1

decls.name: TauCeti.RootPairing.weylGroup.commute_ofIdx_of_isOrthogonal
decls.doc: **Orthogonal roots have commuting reflections** in the Weyl group.
decls.title: Orthogonal roots have commuting reflections
decls.statement:
theorem commute_ofIdx_of_isOrthogonal {i j : ι} (h : P.IsOrthogonal i j) :
    Commute (_root_.RootPairing.weylGroup.ofIdx P i) (_root_.RootPairing.weylGroup.ofIdx P j)

theorem finite_aut_of_span_eq_top

theorem card_subgroup_aut_le_factorial_of_span_eq_top

theorem finite_weylGroup_of_span_eq_top (hspan : Submodule.span R (range P.root) = ⊤) :

theorem card_weylGroup_le_factorial_of_span_eq_top

decls.name: SymmetricPower.map_rel
decls.statement:
theorem map_rel {N : Type*} [AddCommMonoid N] [Module R N] (f : M →ₗ[R] N) :
    addConGen (Rel R ι M) ≤
      AddCon.ker ((mk R ι N).toAddMonoidHom.comp
        (PiTensorProduct.map fun _ : ι => f).toAddMonoidHom)

decls.name: SymmetricPower.map
decls.doc: A linear map induces a linear map on every symmetric tensor power.
decls.statement:
def map {N : Type*} [AddCommMonoid N] [Module R N] (f : M →ₗ[R] N) :
    Sym[R] ι M →ₗ[R] Sym[R] ι N

decls.name: SymmetricPower.map_mk
decls.doc: The map on symmetric powers commutes with the quotient map from the tensor power.
decls.statement:
theorem map_mk {N : Type*} [AddCommMonoid N] [Module R N] (f : M →ₗ[R] N)
    (x : ⨂[R] (_ : ι), M) :
    map f (mk R ι M x) = mk R ι N (PiTensorProduct.map (fun _ : ι => f) x)

decls.name: SymmetricPower.map_tprod
decls.doc: The map induced on symmetric powers sends a pure tensor to the tensor of the images.
decls.statement:
theorem map_tprod {N : Type*} [AddCommMonoid N] [Module R N] (f : M →ₗ[R] N) (m : ι → M) :
    map f (⨂ₛ[R] i, m i) = ⨂ₛ[R] i, f (m i)

decls.name: SymmetricPower.map_id
decls.doc: The map induced by the identity is the identity on the symmetric power.
decls.statement:
theorem map_id :
    map (ι := ι) (LinearMap.id (R := R) (M := M)) = LinearMap.id

decls.name: SymmetricPower.map_comp
decls.doc: Symmetric powers preserve composition of linear maps.
decls.statement:
theorem map_comp {N : Type*} {P : Type*}
    [AddCommMonoid N] [Module R N] [AddCommMonoid P] [Module R P]
    (f : M →ₗ[R] N) (g : N →ₗ[R] P) :
    map (ι := ι) (g.comp f) = (map (ι := ι) g).comp (map (ι := ι) f)

decls.name: SymmetricPower.finite
decls.doc:
A symmetric power indexed by a finite type is finitely generated when the underlying module
is finitely generated.

decls.name: SymmetricPower.toTensorSquare
decls.doc:
The embedding of the symmetric square in the tensor square, given on a pure symmetric
tensor by `x ⊗ₛ y ↦ ⅟2 • (x ⊗ₜ y + y ⊗ₜ x)`.
decls.statement: def toTensorSquare : Sym[R]^2 M →ₗ[R] ⨂[R]^2 M

decls.name: SymmetricPower.toTensorSquare_tprod
decls.doc: The symmetric-square embedding is the half-sum of the two orders on pure tensors.
decls.statement:
theorem toTensorSquare_tprod (f : Fin 2 → M) :
    toTensorSquare R M (⨂ₛ[R] i, f i) =
      (⅟ (2 : R)) •
        (PiTensorProduct.tprod R f +
          PiTensorProduct.tprod R (fun i ↦ f (Equiv.swap 0 1 i)))

decls.name: exteriorPower.toTensorSquare
decls.doc:
The embedding of the exterior square in the tensor square, given on a pure wedge by
`x ∧ y ↦ ⅟2 • (x ⊗ₜ y - y ⊗ₜ x)`.
decls.statement: def toTensorSquare : ⋀[R]^2 M →ₗ[R] ⨂[R]^2 M

decls.name: exteriorPower.toTensorSquare_ιMulti
decls.doc: The exterior-square embedding is the half-difference of the two orders on pure wedges.
decls.statement:
theorem toTensorSquare_ιMulti (f : Fin 2 → M) :
    toTensorSquare R M (ιMulti R 2 f) =
      (⅟ (2 : R)) •
        (PiTensorProduct.tprod R f -
          PiTensorProduct.tprod R (fun i ↦ f (Equiv.swap 0 1 i)))

decls.name: TauCeti.tensorSquareEquivSymmetricExterior
decls.doc:
The tensor square is naturally the direct sum of its symmetric and exterior squares when
`2` is invertible. The forward map sends a tensor to its symmetric quotient and exterior
product.
decls.statement:
def tensorSquareEquivSymmetricExterior :
    (⨂[R]^2 M) ≃ₗ[R] (Sym[R]^2 M) × (⋀[R]^2 M)

decls.name: TauCeti.tensorSquareEquivSymmetricExterior_tprod
decls.doc:
The tensor-square decomposition sends a pure tensor to its symmetric and exterior
classes.
decls.statement:
theorem tensorSquareEquivSymmetricExterior_tprod (f : Fin 2 → M) :
    tensorSquareEquivSymmetricExterior R M (PiTensorProduct.tprod R f) =
      (⨂ₛ[R] i, f i, exteriorPower.ιMulti R 2 f)

decls.name: TauCeti.tensorSquareEquivSymmetricExterior_symm_apply
decls.doc:
The inverse tensor-square decomposition is the sum of the symmetric and exterior
embeddings.
decls.statement:
theorem tensorSquareEquivSymmetricExterior_symm_apply
    (x : (Sym[R]^2M) × (⋀[R]^2 M)) :
    (tensorSquareEquivSymmetricExterior R M).symm x =
      SymmetricPower.toTensorSquare R M x.1 + exteriorPower.toTensorSquare R M x.2

decls.name: TauCeti.LinearMap.trace_pi_of_apply_eq
decls.doc:
The trace of a coordinate-reindexing endomorphism of a finite product is the sum of the
traces on its fixed coordinates.
decls.statement:
theorem LinearMap.trace_pi_of_apply_eq (T : (ι → M) →ₗ[k] (ι → M)) (σ : ι → ι)
    (f : ι → M →ₗ[k] M) (hT : ∀ x i, T x i = f i (x (σ i))) :
    LinearMap.trace k (ι → M) T =
      ∑ i : ι, if σ i = i then LinearMap.trace k M (f i) else 0
